source: Laird (2022) Introduction to Soar, memories overview
finding: Soar has long-term memories beyond rules: semantic (facts as graph structures, cue retrieval, base-level plus spreading activation), episodic (automatic snapshot of the top state at every decision), and RL rules (numeric operator preferences updated by Q-learning or SARSA).
numbers: Episodic stores only changes between episodes; retrieval time for old episodes grows slowly with episode count, recent stays constant. Semantic memory has no automatic learning; the agent stores deliberately.
limits: Overview paper, no benchmark numbers.
agent_relevance: Maps to the schema: S0 class record = semantic store written by an explicit action; episode log = automatic per-step snapshot.
quote: Episodic learning has often been ignored as a learning method because it does not have generalization mechanisms.

source: Laird (2022) Introduction to Soar, section 5 RL
finding: RL in Soar tunes only operator selection. RL preferences are used only when other preferences cannot decide; hard-coded safety rules stay in charge.
numbers: Reward summed from rule-created reward structures; no built-in intrinsic reward; learning and discount rates fixed at agent start; applies per substate (hierarchical RL).
limits: Value learning acts as a tie-breaker under symbolic rules; no numbers given in this overview.
agent_relevance: Matches G1/G2 spirit: a learned score never overrides code-checked rules; use it only to break ties among operators O1-O8.
quote: RL influences operator selection only when the other, non-RL preferences are insufficient for making a decision.

source: Laird (2022) Introduction to Soar, section 7 uses of episodic memory
finding: Lists what episodic memory enables without generalization: virtual sensing, learning action models, retrospective operator evaluation (Mohan and Laird 2013), prospective memory (Li and Laird 2015), replay to debug a course of action.
numbers: Qualitative list; per-study numbers are in the cited papers, which were not opened.
limits: Capabilities listed, not measured here.
agent_relevance: Replaying a stored step sequence to find the failing step fits G2 (revise from real output).

source: Laird (2022) Introduction to Soar, chunking into RL rules
finding: Chunking can create RL rules whose starting value comes from substate evaluation, then experience tunes the value. Chunking can also compile the result of a semantic or episodic recall into a rule.
numbers: Design statement; no benchmark.
limits: Not measured.
agent_relevance: Link between impasse results (S6) and learned operator preference: seed a score from the subgoal, refine from outcomes.
quote: Rules created by chunking will be RL rules that are initialized with whatever evaluation was generated.

source: Nason and Laird (2005) Soar-RL: integrating reinforcement learning with Soar
finding: Founding paper for Soar-RL: numeric preferences as Q-values in rules.
numbers: Not opened this session; figures not recorded.
limits: Known only from the 2022 overview that cites it.

source: Nuxoll and Laird (2012) Enhancing intelligent agents with episodic memory
finding: Founding paper for Soar episodic memory (cue-based retrieval of snapshot episodes).
numbers: Not opened this session; figures not recorded.
limits: Known only via citation in Laird 2022.

source: Wray, Kirk, Laird (2021) Language models as a knowledge source for cognitive agents
finding: Early Soar-group review of using language models as a task-knowledge source. Names accuracy and relevance as the main challenges and proposes the agent learn its own model of what the LM knows.
numbers: One cited rating result: agreement with human raters above 90% in a prior study.
limits: Position and review; no new experiment; text only partly read.
agent_relevance: Treat the LM as a fallible knowledge source whose output is vetted by agent code before it enters memory.
quote: The issues of Accuracy and Relevance are probably the most significant challenges.

source: Kirk, Wray, Lindes, Laird (2024) STARS: improving knowledge extraction from LLMs through agent analysis
finding: A Soar-based agent vets LLM-proposed task knowledge (search tree, analyze and repair, select) before storing it in long-term memory. Template prompting alone gave 35-66% task completion; STARS gave 77-94% with no oversight, 100% with oversight.
numbers: Template prompting: tidy kitchen 52.5%, store groceries 66.7%, organize office 35.7%. STARS: 77.5%, 94.4%, 92.9%. Words the user must give fell 52-68%. Over 70% of raw LLM responses not viable; for one task only 13% were situationally relevant.
limits: Three tasks, one simulated robot setting, GPT-family model, one lab.
agent_relevance: Direct support for a class record built from vetted LLM output: code evaluates and repairs candidates before they enter memory.
quote: Over 70% of responses are not viable.

source: Kirk et al. (2024) STARS: accepted goals under oversight
finding: When the agent pre-filters, humans only confirm or reject. Accepted proposed goals rose from 33% to 69% (kitchen), 62% to 94% (groceries), 18% to 73% (office).
numbers: Compared template prompting with STARS plus oversight on yes/no goal proposals.
limits: Three tasks, one lab.
agent_relevance: Pre-vetting by code raises the quality of what reaches memory more than prompt wording does.

source: Sumers, Yao, Narasimhan, Griffiths (2023) Cognitive Architectures for Language Agents (CoALA)
finding: Maps Soar memories onto language agents: working, episodic, semantic, procedural. Writing to episodic or semantic memory is called much safer than writing to procedural memory (code, prompts, weights).
numbers: Framework paper; survey of agents, no pooled numbers.
limits: Conceptual; categories blur across systems.
agent_relevance: Supports the schema choice: let the agent write class records and episodes freely, and gate any change to its own procedures.
quote: Writing to procedural memory is significantly riskier than writing to episodic or semantic memory.

source: Sumers et al. (2023) CoALA, retrieval and learning gap
finding: CoALA says learning of retrieval itself is not studied in recent language agents; retrieval is a fixed BM25 or dense lookup. It cites reflection over episodic memory to write semantic inferences (Shinn et al. 2023).
numbers: Gap statement as of 2023.
limits: Dated; Memory-R1 (2025) fills part of the gap.
agent_relevance: Learned retrieval or learned operator preference, the Soar-RL analogue, was thin in agents in 2023.

source: Position: Episodic Memory is the Missing Piece for Long-Term LLM Agents (2025)
finding: Argues LLM agents need five episodic properties: long-term storage, explicit reasoning, single-shot learning, instance-specific memory, contextual relations. Says RAG, KV compression, fine-tuning and knowledge editing each miss some.
numbers: Property table (Table 1) and method comparison (Table 2); no experiments.
limits: Argument, not evidence.
agent_relevance: A checklist for the episode log: single-shot write, keep when, why and context with each item.

source: Shinn et al. (2023) Reflexion: language agents with verbal reinforcement learning
finding: Verbal reflections stored in an episodic buffer stand in for RL: failed trials become text hints. On ALFWorld ReAct+Reflexion solved 130 of 134 tasks over 12 trials; ReAct alone stalled between trials 6 and 7.
numbers: ALFWorld 134 tasks, +22% absolute in 12 steps; HotPotQA +20%; HumanEval pass@1 91%. ReAct-only hallucination rate plateaued at 22%.
limits: Needs a binary success signal; memory window of 3 experiences; GPT-3 era models in ALFWorld.
agent_relevance: Verbal RL replaces Soar-RL with text. It needs a real check signal (G2, G3).

source: Shinn et al. (2023) Reflexion, episodic-memory ablation on HotPotQA
finding: Giving the agent only the last trajectory (episodic memory) helped, but adding the self-reflection step gave a further 8% absolute boost.
numbers: 100 HotPotQA questions, CoT with ground-truth context. Reflexion vs episodic-only: +8% absolute.
limits: One run per condition, 100 questions, no interval shown.
agent_relevance: Raw replay is weaker than replay plus a distilled lesson; store the lesson, not only the log.
quote: Self-reflection improves learning by an 8% absolute boost over the episodic memory learning advantage.

source: Park et al. (2023) Generative agents: interactive simulacra of human behavior
finding: Memory stream of observations, retrieval scored by recency, importance and relevance, plus reflections. Ablating memory, planning and reflection lowered human-rated believability.
numbers: 100 raters ranked 5 conditions with TrueSkill: no reflection or planning 25.64 (sd 0.68), crowdworker 22.95, fully ablated 21.21 (sd 0.70); full architecture best. Full vs prior-work baseline d = 8.16. Kruskal-Wallis chi2(4)=150.29, p<0.001.
limits: Believability rating, not task success; short sandbox; agents embellish memories.
agent_relevance: Importance-weighted retrieval is the LLM cousin of Soar base-level activation; shows memory parts add up.
quote: Comparing the condition representing prior work to the full architecture produces a standardized effect size of d = 8.16.

source: Packer et al. (2023) MemGPT: LLMs as operating systems
finding: Model manages paging between a limited main context and external recall and archival stores through function calls. On a deep memory retrieval task it lifts accuracy sharply.
numbers: Accuracy: GPT-3.5 Turbo 38.7% to 66.9% with MemGPT; GPT-4 32.1% to 92.5%; GPT-4 Turbo 35.3% to 93.4%. ROUGE-L GPT-4 0.296 to 0.814.
limits: Only the results table was read, not the full paper; the model decides memory moves itself.
agent_relevance: Analogue of Soar's working versus long-term split, but driven by the model rather than by code.

source: Zhao et al. (2024) ExpeL: LLM agents are experiential learners
finding: Agent stores trajectories and distills cross-task insights (add, edit, remove), then retrieves both. Both parts are needed: insights-only 37% and retrieve-only 38% on HotpotQA, below the combined agent.
numbers: ExpeL matches Reflexion on HotpotQA (40% at R3 vs 39%) and ALFWorld (54% at R3 vs 59%) without retries. ALFWorld: retrieve-only 40.3% to 54.4% over rounds; ExpeL+Reflexion 54.5% to 64.2%. Transfer HotpotQA to FEVER: ReAct 58%, ExpeL 65-70%.
limits: Weaker than Reflexion on WebShop; pool built from the same task family; GPT-3.5/4.
agent_relevance: Closest LLM analogue to episodic plus semantic plus chunking: abstracted insight plus raw episode beats either alone.
quote: Both insight extraction and task similarity retrieval are essential and synergistic.

source: Wang et al. (2023) Voyager: open-ended embodied agent with LLMs
finding: A skill library of verified code (procedural memory) plus automatic curriculum; a skill is committed only after self-verification confirms success. 3.3x more unique items, 2.3x longer distances, tech milestones up to 15.3x faster than prior SOTA.
numbers: Ablations: random curriculum cuts discovered items by 93%; no skill library plateaus in later stages. Tech tree counted over three runs.
limits: Needs a rich API (Mineflayer); GPT-4 code generation; three runs.
agent_relevance: A chunking-like store gated by a check; fits G3: commit only what passed verification.

source: Xiong et al. (2025) How memory management impacts LLM agents: experience-following
finding: Agents copy the outputs of retrieved similar records (experience-following). This causes error propagation (bad stored results degrade later tasks) and misaligned replay (a correct but off-topic record misleads).
numbers: With a strict evaluator, history-based deletion beat an error-free memory baseline on AgentDriver; with a coarse or noisy evaluator the gain disappeared. Periodic deletion helps under task distribution shift.
limits: A few agents (EHRAgent, AgentDriver, synthetic RegAgent); per-figure numbers not extracted.
agent_relevance: Warning for the class record: store only after a trustworthy check and delete by later outcome; later tasks give free quality labels.
quote: Future task evaluations can serve as free quality labels for stored memory.

source: Wu et al. (2025) LongMemEval: benchmarking chat assistants on long-term memory
finding: 500 questions over five abilities (extraction, multi-session reasoning, temporal reasoning, knowledge updates, abstention). Commercial assistants and long-context LLMs lose about 30% accuracy over sustained chats.
numbers: Offline reading GPT-4o 0.9184 accuracy; ChatGPT with GPT-4o 0.5773; Coze with GPT-3.5 0.2474; long-context models drop 30-60% at about 115k tokens.
limits: Chat-assistant domain, not problem solving; LLM-judge grading.
agent_relevance: Episodic recall degrades with length; supports small, curated record stores over dumping history in context.

source: Wu et al. (2025) LongMemEval, design findings
finding: Three-stage view (indexing, retrieval, reading) and optimizations: session decomposition into rounds, fact-augmented key expansion, time-aware query expansion.
numbers: With a GPT-4o reader, round decomposition helped; with Llama 3.1 8B performance was similar to non-decomposed sessions.
limits: Gain depends on the reader model.
agent_relevance: Key episodes by extracted facts (a semantic move) and filter by time (an episodic move).

source: Chhikara et al. (2025) Mem0: production-ready long-term memory
finding: Extract-then-update memory (add, update, delete) beats other memory systems on LoCoMo: 26% relative LLM-judge gain over OpenAI memory, 91% lower p95 latency, over 90% fewer tokens than full context.
numbers: Graph variant about 2% higher than base Mem0. Question types: single-hop, temporal, multi-hop, open-domain.
limits: Authors' own benchmarking and re-runs of baselines; vendor paper.
agent_relevance: A writer module outside the main model can curate a fact store cheaply.
quote: Mem0 attains a 91% lower p95 latency and saves more than 90% token cost.

source: Xu et al. (2025) A-Mem: agentic memory for LLM agents
finding: Zettelkasten-style linked notes that evolve; more than doubles multi-hop performance on LoCoMo (ROUGE-L 44.27 vs 18.09 for the LoCoMo baseline) at about 1,200 tokens per memory operation.
numbers: Token cost reduced from 16,900 to a few thousand via selective top-k retrieval (as stated).
limits: Mem0's re-run with an LLM judge gave different relative numbers; conversational benchmark.
agent_relevance: Linked notes are a spreading-activation analogue, a cheap semantic layer.

source: Yan et al. (2025) Memory-R1: managing and using memories via RL
finding: RL-trained memory manager (add, update, delete, noop) plus answer agent, trained on only 152 QA pairs, beats scripted memory systems on LoCoMo.
numbers: LLaMA-3.1-8B overall F1/judge: LoCoMo RAG 11.41/13.62; A-Mem 29.20/44.76; Mem0 30.41/45.68; MemoryOS 35.04/48.20; Memory-SFT 42.81/58.76; Memory-R1-PPO 41.05/57.54; Memory-R1-GRPO 45.02/62.74. Qwen-2.5-7B GRPO 43.14/61.51.
limits: Trained on LoCoMo only; zero-shot to MSC and LongMemEval; split 152/81/1307. Needs training, which our scaffold avoids.
agent_relevance: The Soar-RL idea (learn which memory operation to pick from reward) works with LLMs; shows value of choosing memory operators well.

source: Yan et al. (2025) Memory-R1, ablation and scaling
finding: Removing any component (manager, answer agent, distillation) lowers scores; a scripted control without RL was clearly worse, with one variant at F1 37.5, B1 30.6, judge 52.9.
numbers: Gains hold across 3B to 14B backbones; GRPO beat PPO on overall F1 by about 4 points for LLaMA-8B.
limits: Authors' own ablation, one benchmark family.
agent_relevance: Deciding what to do with a memory item is learnable and matters; a fixed rule is a weaker baseline.

source: Laird (2012) The Soar Cognitive Architecture (book)
finding: The book the subfield row cites; full account of Soar 9 semantic, episodic and RL modules.
numbers: Not opened this session.
limits: No numbers recorded.

source: Gap note: Soar episodic memory or Soar-RL versus LLM-agent memory
finding: Searches of arXiv and Semantic Scholar found no study running Soar's episodic memory or Soar-RL against an LLM-agent memory on one benchmark.
numbers: Several title searches returned nothing relevant.
limits: Absence of results is not proof; searches were rate-limited.
agent_relevance: Comparisons must rely on analogy; best bridges are STARS (Soar plus LLM) and CoALA.
